# program

```go
import "github.com/danmestas/dagnats/program"
```

Package program is the contract between dagnats and a program: a separately released binary that runs tasks, workflows and services on a dagnats it shares with other programs.

A program declares a Manifest. Its Name is the prefix root of everything it owns: task types and workflows "name.\*", subjects "name.\>", streams "NAME\_\*", buckets "name\_\*". Validate checks a manifest without touching NATS; PermissionsFor derives the NATS permission set dagnats binds to the program's NKey user, which is exactly the crossings the worker SDK and a micro service make plus the program's own resources and nothing wider.

Programs are trusted: these permissions are guardrails against mistakes, not an isolation boundary. A program can still write arbitrary data into the account through JetStream reply reflection \(see Known limitations\), so run only trusted programs until per\-program NATS accounts land \(dagnats\#909\). The guardrails rest on two rules the package enforces:

- A program dials with nats.CustomInboxPrefix\(InboxPrefix\(name\)\), and its permissions grant subscribe on "\_INBOX.\<name\>.\>" only. Every pull fetch, KV watch and JetStream API reply lands on that inbox, so a program does not read another's task bodies or replies. Attach panics on a connection dialed without the prefix.
- The program generates its own NKey \(LoadOrCreateKey\). The seed is written once, mode 0600, and never leaves the process; only the public key is registered.

A program never creates or reconfigures a stream or bucket: a stream config can capture, mirror or republish subjects outside the program's grant. The host creates the manifest's streams and buckets with Provision over its own connection, and the program gets reads, consumers, and key writes on them.

Attach is the one path that calls Program.Start. It takes the Grant the caller obtained \(from registration, the in\-process host, or a literal in tests\), builds a Host, starts the worker that serves the handlers Start registered, and returns a stop func.

Permissions is a plain struct. Converting it to nats\-server options is the server's job, so a program never links nats\-server.

A dagnats node starts serving before it has loaded its program users: they come from the programs bucket, which needs JetStream, which starts with the node. So a node that restarts refuses every program's key for a while \(about 22 seconds on a 3\-node mesh\). Run's connection keeps retrying through that, at first dial and on reconnect, for up to Options.AuthRetryWindow \(AuthRetryWindowDefault, two minutes\), and closes only if the refusals outlast it.

### Known limitations / threat model

Programs on a dagnats are trusted: today they are all the operator's own, the same stance as the coarse\-shared engine buckets. Within that model these gaps are accepted, and they are closed before untrusted \(third\-party\) programs join a dagnats, the same trigger as making nats\_auth: required the default.

- JetStream reply reflection. nats\-server publishes a JetStream API response, a direct get's message and a pull delivery to whatever reply subject the request names, as the account, without checking it against the requester's permissions. So a program can write bytes it chose into any stream or bucket of the account: store them in its own bucket, then direct\-get them with a reply of "$KV.\<bucket\>.\<key\>". Every node therefore derives a program's permissions from its stored manifest and never from a stored permission set. Closed by per\-program NATS accounts, dagnats\#909; TestResidual\_JetStreamReplyWritesForeignBuckets pins the gap and fails once it is closed.
- Push\-consumer delivery. A consumer's deliver subject travels in the JetStream request body, which subject permissions never see, and nats\-server does not check it against the creating user's permissions. So a program can deliver its own stream's messages, or a shared bucket's, onto any subject that has interest, including another program's task or service subjects. KV watches need push consumers, so denying consumer creates is not an option. User permissions inside one account cannot close this; one NATS account per program, or a server\-side check of the deliver subject, will. Tracked as dagnats\#862; TestAttack\_PushConsumerCannotDeliverIntoForeignSubjects is the proof, skipped until then.
- Inbox forgery. Micro services reply by publishing to the caller's inbox, so every program may publish on "\_INBOX.\>". Inbox names are not secret: one process's inboxes share a prefix and are numbered in sequence, so a single reply subject seen from program beta \(on a shared protocol, say\) lets program alpha write forged replies into beta's next inboxes. Reading stays confined to the program's own "\_INBOX.\<name\>.\>". Tracked as dagnats\#862 and closed by the same fix as push\-consumer delivery: accounts or a server\-side check.
- Name\-gated grants. Consumer delete on shared buckets and next, ack and create on STICKY\_TASKS are gated only by consumer names: random NUIDs, and for sticky consumers 128 bits from crypto/rand, which a program can neither list nor read from any bucket, reply or advisory.
- Protocol ownership. Validate cannot see other programs, so a protocol such as "beta.x" declared by program alpha would be granted under beta's prefix. Registration must check ownership both ways: a protocol under a registered program's prefix, and a program registering a name some protocol already sits under.

## Constants

<a name="RegisterSubject"></a>RegisterSubject is the request subject a program registers on. The registration connection is anonymous and dialed with nats.CustomInboxPrefix\(JoinInboxPrefix\), so that in a required\-auth server its join user sees registration replies and nothing else.

```go
const (
    RegisterSubject = "api.programs.register"
    JoinInboxPrefix = "_JOIN"
)
```

<a name="RefusedRequestInvalid"></a>Refusal codes. Each reaches the program as an \*ErrRefused from Run.

```go
const (
    RefusedRequestInvalid      = "request_invalid"
    RefusedNameInvalid         = "name_invalid"
    RefusedNameTaken           = "name_taken"
    RefusedManifestChanged     = "manifest_changed"
    RefusedJoinKeyInvalid      = "join_key_invalid"
    RefusedJoinKeyExhausted    = "join_key_exhausted"
    RefusedBudgetExceeded      = "budget_exceeded"
    RefusedVersionIncompatible = "version_incompatible"
    RefusedProtocolClash       = "protocol_clash"
    RefusedProtocolNotAllowed  = "protocol_not_allowed"
    RefusedConfirmExpired      = "confirm_expired"
    // RefusedJoinKeyRequiredToWiden: an update adds a protocol or a read
    // of another program's bucket, and the request carries no join key
    // that is usable and covers it.
    RefusedJoinKeyRequiredToWiden = "join_key_required_to_widen"
)
```

<a name="AuthRetryWindowDefault"></a>AuthRetryWindowDefault is how long a program's connection rides out the server refusing its key. A node serves clients before its watch of the programs bucket has loaded its program users \(the bucket needs JetStream, which starts with the node\), so a node that restarts refuses every program key for a while: about 22 seconds on a 3\-node mesh.

```go
const AuthRetryWindowDefault = 2 * time.Minute
```

<a name="ConfirmSubjectWildcard"></a>ConfirmSubjectWildcard is what the registration service answers.

```go
const ConfirmSubjectWildcard = confirmSubjectPrefix + "*"
```

<a name="ErrRelayUnavailable"></a>ErrRelayUnavailable is returned by Attach, and so Run, when no dagnats control plane answers the program relay: the server is older than v0.0.42 or runs without its NATS API. A host can test for it with errors.Is to tell an operator to upgrade or start the dagnats server.

```go
var ErrRelayUnavailable = natsutil.ErrRelayUnavailable
```

<a name="Attach"></a>
## func [Attach](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/attach.go#L41-L43>)

```go
func Attach(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, prog Program, g Grant) (stop func(context.Context) error, err error)
```

Attach is the one path that calls prog.Start. It takes the Grant the caller already obtained \(registration, the in\-process host, or a literal in tests\), builds a Host, calls Start, and then starts the worker that serves the handlers Start registered through Host.Handle. Each dispatch runs under a recover, so a panicking handler fails its task permanently instead of killing the process.

nc must have been dialed with nats.CustomInboxPrefix\(InboxPrefix\(name\)\); Attach panics otherwise, because the program's permissions grant no other inbox and every reply would time out.

The returned stop func stops the worker \(draining in\-flight tasks\), then calls prog.Stop once; later calls return the first result. When Start fails, Attach returns its error without calling Stop. When the worker fails to start, Attach calls Stop and returns both errors.

<a name="Provision"></a>
## func [Provision](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/provision.go#L28>)

```go
func Provision(ctx context.Context, js jetstream.JetStream, m Manifest, g Grant) error
```

Provision creates or updates the manifest's streams and buckets at the sizes in g. The host calls it over its own connection: a program's permissions grant no stream create or update, because a stream config can capture, mirror or republish subjects the program may not touch. Idempotent.

An existing stream or bucket keeps every field the manifest does not own \(Discard, MaxMsgs, DenyDelete, MaxValueSize, compression and the rest\): only subjects, size, age limit, history, replicas and storage are written over its live config, so adopting a stream an operator made does not reset it to defaults.

Those owned fields always come from the manifest and Grant, so a limit an operator tightened by hand \(MaxBytes, MaxAge, TTL, History, Replicas\) is undone by the next Provision. That stays within the Grant, so no data is lost. A bucket field KeyValueConfig cannot express, such as its stream's MaxMsgs, is reset to the KV default.

<a name="Host"></a>
## type [Host](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/manifest.go#L96-L104>)

Host is what Start receives. It is data: the connection the program was attached with, its Grant, a logger tagged with its name, and Handle, which registers a task handler on the worker Attach runs.

```go
type Host struct {
    Conn   *nats.Conn
    Grant  Grant
    Logger *slog.Logger
    // Handle registers fn for a declared task type. Attach wraps it in
    // a per-dispatch recover and starts consuming once Start returns.
    // Calling it after Start returns, or for an undeclared type, panics.
    Handle func(taskType string, fn worker.HandlerFunc, opts ...worker.HandlerOption)
}
```

<a name="LoadOrCreateKey"></a>
### func [LoadOrCreateKey](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/keys.go#L34>)

```go
func LoadOrCreateKey(seedPath string) (Key, error)
```

LoadOrCreateKey returns the identity stored at seedPath, generating a user key pair and writing its seed there \(mode 0600, exclusive create\) when the file does not exist. An existing seed is read, never rewritten; one readable by group or others is refused. The parent directory must exist.

<a name="Manifest"></a>
## type [Manifest](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/manifest.go#L16-L50>)

Manifest is everything dagnats needs to admit a program. Name is the prefix root: task types and workflow names "name.\*", subjects "name.\>", streams "NAME\_\*", buckets "name\_\*".

```go
type Manifest struct {
    // Name is [a-z][a-z0-9]{1,31}. It may not shadow an engine subject
    // root, stream or bucket (Validate lists them).
    Name string
    // Version is the program's own version, informational.
    Version string
    // Dagnats is the semver range the program was built for, e.g.
    // ">=0.0.35 <0.1.0". Registration evaluates it.
    Dagnats string
    // TaskTypes are the task types the program's worker handles, each
    // "name.<rest>". Host.Handle refuses any other.
    TaskTypes []string
    // Workflows optionally lists fixed workflow names the program
    // registers, each "name.<rest>". It is documentation, not a limit:
    // api.p.<name>.workflows.register accepts any name under "name.",
    // including ones made up at runtime.
    Workflows []string
    Streams   []StreamSpec
    Buckets   []BucketSpec
    // Reads are other programs' KV buckets this program may read (get
    // and watch, never write), each a full bucket name such as
    // "tools_registry" under ANOTHER program's prefix. Not the
    // program's own buckets (those already get full access) and not an
    // engine bucket. Whether the owner program exists is not checkable
    // by Validate: an entry for a bucket nobody owns grants nothing
    // usable. A reader's watcher.Stop returns a timeout error after ~5s
    // (consumer delete is denied); the server reaps the consumer itself.
    Reads []string
    // Protocols are shared subject roots the program speaks, e.g.
    // "tool.exec": publish and subscribe on the root and below it.
    Protocols []string
    // Console links the program from the dagnats console nav; nil for
    // none.
    Console *Link
}
```

<a name="Options"></a>
## type [Options](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/run.go#L22-L43>)

Options is where a connected program finds its dagnats.

```go
type Options struct {
    // URL is the nats:// address of the server the program dials.
    URL string
    // SeedPath is where the program's NKey seed lives; created on the
    // first run, mode 0600.
    SeedPath string
    // JoinKey is presented at registration. Empty is accepted only by
    // a dagnats whose NATS clients need no login (open mode).
    JoinKey string
    // NATSOptions are applied to both of Run's connections before Run's
    // own (inbox prefix, login, name, reconnect policy, close handler),
    // so they cannot override those. A ClosedHandler here is chained,
    // not replaced.
    NATSOptions []nats.Option
    // AuthRetryWindow is how long the program's connection keeps
    // retrying while the server refuses its key, at first dial and on
    // reconnect: a restarting node serves before it has loaded its
    // program users. Refusals that outlast it close the connection for
    // good (Running.Done), as for a key that was removed. Zero means
    // AuthRetryWindowDefault.
    AuthRetryWindow time.Duration
}
```

```go
func OptionsFromEnv(name string) Options
```

OptionsFromEnv reads \<NAME\>\_DAGNATS\_URL, \<NAME\>\_SEED and \<NAME\>\_JOIN\_KEY, with NAME the program name in upper case: notify reads NOTIFY\_DAGNATS\_URL. The URL defaults to nats://127.0.0.1:4222 and the seed to ./\<name\>.seed.

<a name="Permissions"></a>
## type [Permissions](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/permissions.go#L29-L32>)

Permissions is a plain permission set for one program's NATS user. The server converts it to nats\-server's own type, so a program never links nats\-server.

There is deliberately no response permission \(allow\_responses\): the server grants it for any delivered message with a reply subject, whoever sent it, so a program could publish to itself with a forged reply and "respond" anywhere. Replies go out under Publish "\_INBOX.\>" instead. A program still reads only its own "\_INBOX.\<name\>.\>", but it can write into another's inboxes: see "Known limitations / threat model" in the package doc \(\#862\).

```go
type Permissions struct {
    Publish   SubjectPermission
    Subscribe SubjectPermission
}
```

<a name="PermissionsFor"></a>
### func [PermissionsFor](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/permissions.go#L73>)

```go
func PermissionsFor(m Manifest) Permissions
```

PermissionsFor derives the NATS permission set for a manifest: every crossing the worker SDK and a micro service make, the program's own subjects, streams and buckets, its protocols, its own output under "stream.p.\<name\>.\>" and "logs.p.\<name\>.\>", and subscribe on "\_INBOX.\<name\>.\>" and nothing wider. Pure. Panics on a manifest that fails Validate: permissions for an invalid manifest are meaningless.

These are guardrails against a trusted program's mistakes, not an isolation boundary: JetStream reply reflection lets a program write any stream or bucket of the account \(package doc, dagnats\#909\).

Residual: next, ack and create on a STICKY\_TASKS consumer are granted for any consumer name, so a program holding a sibling's name could pull, ack or reconfigure it. The names are unguessable and never disclosed \(stickyPublish\), and TestPermissions\_StickyConsumerNamesNotDisclosed pins the disclosure surfaces.

}

<a name="RegisterReply"></a>
## type [RegisterReply](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/register.go#L70-L75>)

RegisterReply is the reply: a Grant, Refused or Error. Error is a server fault \(a KV write failed\), not a refusal, and may succeed on retry. Confirm, when set, is the subject the program must confirm on after logging in with its key: a new registration is pending until then, and a manifest change is applied only then \(Grant may be nil\).

```go
type RegisterReply struct {
    Confirm string      `json:"confirm,omitempty"`
    Grant   *Grant      `json:"grant,omitempty"`
    Refused *ErrRefused `json:"refused,omitempty"`
    Error   string      `json:"error,omitempty"`
}
```

<a name="Running"></a>
## type [Running](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/running.go#L14-L27>)

Running is a program Run attached. Stop ends it; Done reports when it ended, including when its connection closed for good on its own.

```go
type Running struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="Run"></a>
### func [Run](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/run.go#L81>)

```go
func Run(ctx context.Context, prog Program, opts Options) (*Running, error)
```

Run is the connected placement. It loads or creates the program's NKey at opts.SeedPath, registers with dagnats over an anonymous connection \(a restart with the same key and manifest gets the stored Grant back\), dials as the program's own user with its inbox prefix, and Attaches. A refusal is returned as an \*ErrRefused before any stream, consumer or handler exists.

The program's connection reconnects forever, so a dagnats that is down for a long upgrade does not strand the process. It also rides out a node that refuses its key while restarting \(Options.AuthRetryWindow\), and closes only if the refusals outlast that window. Hosts should still watch Running.Done and exit when it fires, so their supervisor restarts them: it reports a connection closed for good.

<a name="Running.Done"></a>
### func \(\*Running\) [Done](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/running.go#L58>)

```go
func (r *Running) Done() <-chan error
```

Done receives exactly one value and is then closed: nil after Stop, or the reason the connection closed for good without Stop. A host should exit on a non\-nil value so its supervisor restarts it; the program is no longer reachable.

<a name="Running.Stop"></a>
### func \(\*Running\) [Stop](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/running.go#L39>)

```go
func (r *Running) Stop(ctx context.Context) error
```

Stop drains the worker, calls prog.Stop and closes the connection. It makes no control\-plane request, so it works while dagnats is down. Later calls return the first result.

<a name="StreamSpec"></a>
## type [StreamSpec](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/manifest.go#L56-L64>)

StreamSpec declares one of the program's own JetStream streams. The host creates it \(Provision\); the program only reads and consumes it. Its MaxBytes is resolved by dagnats from the fraction and floor and handed back in Grant.StreamMaxBytes.

```go
type StreamSpec struct {
    Name string // "NAME_<REST>", upper case
    // Subjects the stream captures, each under the program's "name."
    // prefix; wildcards allowed.
    Subjects         []string
    MaxBytesFraction float64
    MaxBytesFloor    int64
    MaxAge           time.Duration
}
```

<a name="SubjectPermission"></a>
## type [SubjectPermission](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/program/permissions.go#L13-L16>)

SubjectPermission is one direction's allow and deny subject lists, with NATS wildcard semantics. A subject is permitted when an Allow entry matches it and no Deny entry does.

```go
type SubjectPermission struct {
    Allow []string
    Deny  []string
}
```
